argument: The nontrivial zeta zeros include an unbounded sequence of critical-line heights.
A fixed-radius centered inversion would send those heights to a sequence tending to 0.
The inversion is injective, so invariance would give distinct transformed zeros accumulating at s=1/2.
Zeta is analytic and nonzero at s=1/2, so the identity theorem forbids that accumulation.
analytic_obstruction.center_nonzero_analytic_reason: eta(1/2) is a positive alternating-series sum and zeta(1/2)=eta(1/2)/(1-sqrt(2)) is therefore nonzero
analytic_obstruction.scope: This rules out global invariance of the zeta zero set under any one fixed positive centered radius; it does not challenge the exact coordinate geometry.

transformed_function_caveat.center_status: s=1/2 becomes an essential singularity because I_R has a pole there and zeta has an essential singularity at infinity
transformed_function_caveat.interpretation: this is a new representation of zeta after precomposition, not a symmetry or permutation of the original zeta zero set
transformed_function_caveat.zero_accumulation_status: zeros of the transformed function may accumulate at that singularity

allowed_claim_language: The centered Mobius identities and rational shell identities hold exactly externally.
The strict graph may witness rational precursor edges and component nodes.
A finite Hasse calculation can reject preservation of the supplied near-zero at its centered-inversion image.
A fixed-radius global zeta-zero symmetry is analytically obstructed by zero accumulation at the center.
disallowed_claim_language: Do not claim that the current strict positive-spine runtime contains complex numbers, U(1), Mobius maps, or zeta.
Do not identify the centered involution with the quarter-turn C4 action; only the four-point set is shared.
Do not identify all rational-coordinate shell points with roots of unity.
Do not treat the exact reformulation abs(w(rho))=1 as evidence for RH; it is equivalent to Re(rho)=1/2.
Do not promote a formal interaction branch without repeated graph-native construction edges and a predictive test.

phase_to_pair_projection_edge.reason: the rational graph has no domain-tagged complex pair or projection-edge type

rational_multiplication_contrast.meaning: Core rational multiplication of 1/4 by 1/4 targets 1/16; it must not be aliased to i*i.

complex_calibration.unit_modulus_meaning: absolute value 1 in U(1), not the one-class integer quotient Z/1Z

alignment.operand_rule: positive-spine strict corpus: only confirmed positive-spine iterations may be operands

coordinate_loci.u_unit_shell_in_w_plane: Re(w)=0, including the projective infinity endpoint
coordinate_loci.w_unit_shell_in_s_plane: Re(s)=1/2 in the extended plane; the finite Mobius action is defined on the punctured line s!=1/2
coordinate_loci.w_unit_shell_in_u_plane: Re(u)=0, including the projective infinity endpoint
coordinate_loci.warning: The centered circle and critical line are different invariant loci; modulus-one is coordinate-dependent, not Mobius-invariant language.

exact_identities.critical_line_action: the finite punctured line s=1/2+it, t!=0, maps to itself by t->1/(4t); s=1/2 exchanges with projective infinity

matrix_lift.reading: The order-four homogeneous lift projects to an involution because a matrix and its negative define the same Mobius map.
matrix_lift.representative_status: order four belongs to the chosen real determinant-one representative; ordinary matrix order is not invariant under arbitrary complex scalar rescaling

graph_shell_audit.reading: The current strict positive-spine corpus can witness the rational precursor 1/n. Under its aligned operand policy, the reciprocal landing and shell components are inspected rather than reused as operands, and this runtime has no complex-pair or Mobius edge type.

summary.rh_status: abs(w(rho))=1 is an exact restatement of critical-line membership, not new evidence for the Riemann hypothesis

q_mod_z_phase_model.coordinate_status: the four units are landmarks in the normalized external w/U(1) plane; the raw s-plane map does not preserve the raw set {1,i,-1,-i}
q_mod_z_phase_model.order_change_example: phase 1/3 has order 3 and maps to phase 1/6 of order 6
q_mod_z_phase_model.warning: Centered inversion preserves the C4 set but is not the existing quarter-turn C4 action.

example.reason: 3/5+4i/5 is not an algebraic integer, hence cannot be a root of unity.

set_relation.reading: The inversion preserves both rational skeletons separately; generic rational-coordinate shell points are not roots of unity.

functional_reflection_on_critical_line_c.meaning: at sigma=1/2, s->1-s equals complex conjugation; this is a conjugation control, not an independent evaluation of the full functional equation

zeta_evaluations.method: finite external binary64 Hasse/eta approximation; cutoff comparisons are empirical and are not rigorous error bounds
